builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Accelerate Bench: Evaluating Agents for Application-Level Program Optimization
summary: This benchmark replaces ad-hoc or synthetic evaluations of coding agents with standardized, application-level CPU optimization tasks derived from scientific workloads. It requires infrastructure to execute programs and verify correctness, introducing overhead in environment setup and compute time. Coordination failures can occur because identical source code varies from 0.29x to 2.12x depending on build settings, and individual optimizations may yield 1.01x or 6.4x depending on interaction with other changes.
rationale: The reader can use this benchmark to evaluate and select coding agents for performance-critical code optimization using standard hardware, without needing to train models or manage clusters.

claims.statement: This benchmark replaces ad-hoc or synthetic evaluations of coding agents with standardized, application-level CPU optimization tasks derived from scientific workloads. It requires infrastructure to execute programs and verify correctness, introducing overhead in environment setup and compute time. Coordination failures can occur because identical source code varies from 0.29x to 2.12x depending on build settings, and individual optimizations may yield 1.01x or 6.4x depending on interaction with other changes.
Leading agents achieve at least 2x speedup on 22 or more of the 32 tasks, while the other fourteen reach 2x on only 8 to 17 tasks.
